title_en: Yu Zhongmin v. Tian Yinxian and Liu Ying — dispute over confirmation of house ownership

full_text_en:
Yu Zhongmin v. Tian Yinxian and Liu Ying — dispute over confirmation of house ownership

Ruling Summary

The purpose of a third-party revocation action is to revoke the part of the original judgment that is adverse to the third party. Unlike retrial proceedings, a third-party revocation action does not adjudicate the claims of the original parties.

Plaintiff: Yu Zhongmin, female, 49 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Defendant: Tian Yinxian, male, 50 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Defendant: Liu Ying, female, 33 years old, Han Chinese, domiciled in Nanshan District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

The plaintiff, Yu Zhongmin, filed an action with the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants, Tian Yinxian and Liu Ying, concerning a dispute over confirmation of ownership.

Plaintiff's Allegations

Yu Zhongmin alleged that she and defendant Tian Yinxian married in 1988 and had two daughters. In October 2007, Tian Yinxian purchased the subject property in the name of a third party, Li Mou, and paid RMB 10.18 million and RMB 300,000 in succession as the purchase price. Later, Li Mou was transferred away from Shanghai, and the advance notice registration of the subject property was made in the name of Tian Yinxian. On April 2, 2009, without Yu Zhongmin's knowledge, Tian Yinxian unilaterally registered the subject property in the name of defendant Liu Ying. On July 4, 2011, Tian Yinxian issued a written statement confirming that he had gifted the subject property he purchased to Liu Ying. On December 7, 2011, Yu Zhongmin filed an action with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court against Tian Yinxian and Liu Ying, seeking a declaration that the gift was invalid. On February 8, 2012, Liu Ying filed a jurisdictional objection with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court. The Dalian Intermediate People's Court ruled on February 16, 2012, to dismiss the jurisdictional objection. Liu Ying appealed, and the Liaoning High People's Court ruled on May 17, 2012, to dismiss the appeal. On May 14, 2012, Tian Yinxian filed an action with the Jiading District People's Court concerning the subject property. The Jiading District People's Court rendered a civil judgment on August 9, 2012, [(2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504], confirming that Tian Yinxian held a 60% ownership share in the subject property located in Jiading District, Shanghai. Yu Zhongmin believed that the purchase price for the subject property was entirely paid by Tian Yinxian and constituted common property of Yu Zhongmin and Tian Yinxian. Tian Yinxian's unilateral gift of it to Liu Ying infringed upon Yu Zhongmin's lawful rights and interests. The two defendants maliciously colluded to conceal from the Jiading District People's Court the fact that Yu Zhongmin had already filed an action in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court regarding the validity of the gift, thereby causing the plaintiff to be unable to participate in that case. Furthermore, the effective civil judgment of the Jiading District People's Court infringed upon Yu Zhongmin's lawful rights and interests. Therefore, Yu Zhongmin requested the revocation of the civil judgment [(2012) Jia Min San Min Chu Zi No. 504] rendered by the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai on August 9, 2012.

Defendant Tian Yinxian's Defense

Tian Yinxian argued against the revocation and requested that the plaintiff's claim be dismissed. He stated that he and defendant Liu Ying had a cooperative investment in the subject property and had agreed on the distribution of proceeds. There was no malicious collusion with Liu Ying. The subject property was originally registered in Liu Ying's name, and confirming that Tian Yinxian held a 60% ownership share did not infringe upon Yu Zhongmin's rights.

Defendant Liu Ying's Defense

Liu Ying argued that there was no issue of a gift; defendant Tian Yinxian had never obtained any real right in the subject property. The relationship with Tian Yinxian concerning the subject property was a cooperative investment. Liu Ying had already paid Tian Yinxian RMB 2.7 million in accordance with the agreement between them, which Tian Yinxian had acknowledged. The plaintiff's claim for revocation was time-barred. Liu Ying had submitted the effective judgment in dispute to Yu Zhongmin for cross-examination during the Dalian Intermediate People's Court hearing on August 30, 2012. The new Civil Procedure Law came into effect on January 1, 2013. Yu Zhongmin should have brought the revocation action by June 30, 2013, but failed to do so. The statute of limitations for a revocation action is not subject to suspension or interruption. In conclusion, Liu Ying requested that Yu Zhongmin's claim be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance

The plaintiff, Yu Zhongmin, and defendant Tian Yinxian are husband and wife, having registered their marriage on December 28, 1988, and they remain married. Defendant Liu Ying gave birth to a non-marital daughter with Tian Yinxian in 2009.

In October 2007, Tian Yinxian purchased the subject property from Shanghai Xin'anting Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Xin'anting Company") in the name of a third party, Li Mou. Before October 24, 2007, Tian Yinxian paid RMB 10.18 million as the purchase price through Li Mou and others. The property was registered for advance notice in Li Mou's name on October 19, 2007 (this registration was cancelled on May 28, 2008). Tian Yinxian paid RMB 300,000 to Xin'anting Company on April 8, 2008. Later, due to changes in the measured area, Xin'anting Company refunded RMB 26,337 to Tian Yinxian in two installments. The subject property was registered for advance notice in Tian Yinxian's name on June 6, 2008. On June 8, 2008, the two defendants signed a cooperation agreement, stipulating that they would jointly fund the purchase of the subject property; the property title would be registered in Liu Ying's name but would be jointly owned by both; after the return of their respective capital contributions, the proceeds would be jointly owned by both. On January 25, 2009, Tian Yinxian issued a receipt, acknowledging receipt of RMB 2.7 million from Liu Ying as part of the purchase price, stating that future taxes, property management fees, and other expenses would be borne by Liu Ying, that the property rights would be jointly owned by both (Tian Yinxian holding 60%, Liu Ying holding 40%), that both parties would temporarily refrain from using the property, and that upon sale, each party's actual capital contribution would be returned first, with the remaining proceeds to be split equally (50% each). The disposal of the property required the full consent of both parties. On March 13, 2009, Tian Yinxian and Xin'anting Company signed an agreement to cancel the pre-sale contract and the advance notice registration for the subject property, and the registration was cancelled on March 16, 2009. On March 24, 2009, Liu Ying and Xin'anting Company signed a "Shanghai Commercial Housing Sale Contract" for the subject property. The subject property was registered in Liu Ying's name on April 20, 2009. On July 4, 2011, Tian Yinxian issued a statement confirming that he had gifted the subject property to Liu Ying in April 2009. On November 5, 2011, Tian Yinxian issued an explanation concerning the purchase process of the subject property, stating that he had purchased it in Li Mou's name, after which Li Mou and Xin'anting Company rescinded the pre-sale contract; he (Tian) then signed a new pre-sale contract with Xin'anting Company and completed advance notice registration; in March 2009, he gifted the subject property to his girlfriend Liu Ying, and with the cooperation of Xin'anting Company, the pre-sale contract and advance notice registration were cancelled; Liu Ying then signed a new sale contract with Xin'anting Company and completed the property title registration; Liu Ying herself had not paid any of the purchase price.

On December 7, 2011, plaintiff Yu Zhongmin filed an action with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court. Alleging that during the marriage, defendant Tian Yinxian had concealed from her the fact that he had repeatedly used substantial amounts of marital property to purchase property for defendant Liu Ying, and that after learning of this she had demanded its return without success, Yu Zhongmin sought an order requiring the two defendants to return RMB 25 million. After the Dalian Intermediate People's Court accepted the case, Liu Ying raised a jurisdictional objection during the defense period, arguing that the case involved a real estate dispute and requesting that it be transferred to a Shanghai court. After review, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court held that the nature of the dispute concerned the validity of a gift and did not fall within the category of real estate disputes subject to exclusive jurisdiction; it therefore dismissed the motion. Defendant Liu Ying appealed, and the Liaoning High People's Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the ruling.

During the appeal of the jurisdictional objection, on May 14, 2012, defendant Tian Yinxian filed an action against defendant Liu Ying with the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai, seeking a judgment confirming that he held a 60% ownership share in the subject property located at No. 4, Lane 6777, Boyuan Road, Jiading District, Shanghai (hereinafter "the subject property"). During the proceedings, Tian Yinxian and Liu Ying jointly concealed from the Jiading District People's Court the facts that Yu Zhongmin had already filed an action concerning the subject property in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court, her identity, and the relationship between the two defendants. On August 9, 2012, the Jiading District People's Court rendered a civil judgment [(2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504], confirming that Tian Yinxian held a 60% ownership share in the subject property located at No. 4, Lane 6777, Boyuan Road, Jiading District, Shanghai. Neither party appealed, and the judgment became effective.

On August 30, 2012, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court held a hearing in the case concerning Yu Zhongmin's action against Tian Yinxian and Liu Ying regarding the gift contract. During the hearing, Yu Zhongmin amended her claims, seeking a declaration that the gift between the two defendants was invalid, an order requiring Liu Ying to return the gifted property and to restore the registration of the property to the name of Yu Zhongmin and Tian Yinxian. On the same day, Liu Ying submitted the civil judgment [(2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504] of the Jiading District People's Court as evidence for Yu Zhongmin's cross-examination. On July 4, 2013, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment [(2012) Da Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3], affirming that Tian Yinxian's gift of the subject property to Liu Ying was invalid and ordering Liu Ying to transfer the property title back to Tian Yinxian or to plaintiff Yu Zhongmin. After this judgment was rendered, Liu Ying appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court on July 20, 2013. Following clarification by the Liaoning High People's Court, Yu Zhongmin, on the ground that the civil judgment [(2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504] of the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai had infringed her lawful rights and interests, filed an action with the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai on September 26, 2013, seeking the revocation of that judgment.

On October 23, 2013, the Liaoning High People's Court rendered a civil ruling [(2013) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 216], ruling to revoke the Dalian Intermediate People's Court's civil judgment [(2012) Da Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3] and dismissing plaintiff Yu Zhongmin's complaint.

It was further found that defendant Liu Ying confirmed that the purchase price paid to Xin'anting Company was entirely paid by defendant Tian Yinxian and that she had not paid any portion of the price to Xin'anting Company. Neither of the two defendants currently uses the subject property. The subject property is still registered in Liu Ying's name. During the proceedings, upon the application of plaintiff Yu Zhongmin, the Jiading District People's Court issued a judicial seizure order against the subject property.

During the hearing, plaintiff Yu Zhongmin argued that if the original judgment were revoked, the ownership of the subject property should be confirmed as jointly owned by plaintiff and defendant Tian Yinxian, and requested that defendant Liu Ying return her share of the gifted property. Tian Yinxian argued that if the revocation were granted, he should hold 100% ownership of the subject property. Liu Ying opposed the revocation.

Opinion of the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance

The court identified the following issues: (1) the statute of limitations; (2) whether the original judgment should be revoked; and (3) the disposition after revocation.

1. *Statute of limitations.* Although plaintiff Yu Zhongmin learned of the original judgment on August 30, 2012, at that time the Dalian Intermediate People's Court had not yet rendered a decision on her action against the two defendants concerning the validity of the gift of the subject property. Therefore, it was uncertain whether Yu Zhongmin's civil rights and interests would actually be harmed by the original judgment. The first-instance judgment of the Dalian Intermediate People's Court supported Yu Zhongmin's claims. It was only after defendant Liu Ying appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court on July 20, 2013, and upon clarification by the Liaoning High People's Court, that Yu Zhongmin became aware that her civil rights and interests could be harmed by the original judgment. The Liaoning High People's Court subsequently revoked the Dalian court's judgment and dismissed Yu Zhongmin's complaint, which is when her civil rights and interests actually suffered harm. Accordingly, the statute of limitations should run from the time Yu Zhongmin knew or should have known that her civil rights and interests would be harmed. Therefore, Yu Zhongmin's action was not time-barred.

2. *Whether the original judgment should be revoked.* Defendant Tian Yinxian's act of purchasing the subject property with his own funds occurred during the subsistence of his marriage to plaintiff Yu Zhongmin. According to the Marriage Law of the PRC, this purchase should be considered as using marital property. After Tian Yinxian purchased the property and obtained the quasi-property right through advance notice registration, he, without Yu Zhongmin's consent, unilaterally cancelled the advance notice registration and registered the property in defendant Liu Ying's name, even though Liu Ying had not paid any of the purchase price. This infringed upon Yu Zhongmin's rights as a spouse to own and equally dispose of marital property. The original judgment, which determined the ownership of the subject property based on the property being registered in Liu Ying's name and the confirmation by the two defendants of Tian Yinxian's share, infringed upon Yu Zhongmin's civil rights and interests and should be revoked.

3. *Disposition of the claims of the original plaintiff Tian Yinxian after revocation of the original judgment.* Even after plaintiff Yu Zhongmin had already filed an action concerning the gift of the subject property, the original plaintiff, Tian Yinxian, brought an action before the Jiading District People's Court seeking confirmation of a 60% ownership share in the subject property. He and defendant Liu Ying intentionally concealed from the court the facts that Yu Zhongmin had already filed an action in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court, her identity, and the relationship between the two defendants. They attempted to obstruct the proceedings in the related case in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court through litigation, thereby infringing upon plaintiff Yu Zhongmin's lawful rights and interests. This constituted malicious litigation. Therefore, the claims of the original plaintiff, Tian Yinxian, should be dismissed.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 56 and Article 112 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 17 of the Marriage Law of the PRC, the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai rendered the following judgment on October 22, 2014:

1.  Revoke the civil judgment [(2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504].
2.  Dismiss the claims of the original plaintiff, Tian Yinxian.

Liu Ying, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court.

Appellant Liu Ying's Arguments

Liu Ying argued that she had paid RMB 1.8 million of the purchase price and had also transferred a BMW sedan valued at RMB 700,000 to appellee Tian Yinxian as part payment, so she had actually paid the purchase price. The appellee Yu Zhongmin's action in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court was unrelated to the subject property, and Liu Ying did not conceal the fact of that lawsuit. Tian Yinxian never obtained ownership of the subject property; even if there was a gift, it was merely of money. The statute of limitations for a revocation action runs from the date the party knows or should know of the facts. The statute of limitations in this case has expired. The statements and gift confirmation issued by Tian Yinxian to Yu Zhongmin were not acknowledged by Tian Yinxian or Liu Ying, and there was no evidence to support them in the first instance. There was no malicious collusion between Liu Ying and Tian Yinxian; Yu Zhongmin and Tian Yinxian were husband and wife, an interest community, who colluded to infringe upon Liu Ying's lawful rights and interests. The first-instance judgment contained errors in both fact-finding and legal application, and Liu Ying requested its revocation on appeal.

Appellee Yu Zhongmin's Defense

Yu Zhongmin argued that the first-instance judgment correctly found the facts and applied the law, and requested that the appeal be dismissed and the judgment affirmed.

Appellee Tian Yinxian did not submit a defense.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

Opinion of the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court on Appeal

The subject property was purchased by appellee Tian Yinxian during the subsistence of his marriage to appellee Yu Zhongmin. Tian Yinxian's disposal of the subject property without Yu Zhongmin's consent affected Yu Zhongmin's civil rights and interests in the property. In the civil action numbered (2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504, Tian Yinxian and appellant Liu Ying failed to inform the original court that Yu Zhongmin had already filed an action concerning the subject property in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court, which caused Yu Zhongmin to be unable to participate in that case for reasons not attributable to her. Evidence provided by Yu Zhongmin, including the statement and explanation of the purchase process issued by Tian Yinxian, as well as the proceedings in the Dalian Intermediate People's Court and the Liaoning High People's Court, sufficiently demonstrates that the content of the effective civil judgment [(2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504] was erroneous and infringed upon her civil rights and interests. Yu Zhongmin's request for revocation of that judgment should be supported in accordance with law.

Regarding the statute of limitations issue, the first-instance court has already addressed it with sufficient reasoning, and this court concurs. The appellant Liu Ying's argument on this point is inconsistent with the facts and is not adopted by this court.

Because the appellee Yu Zhongmin's claim in the original instance of this case was precisely to revoke the civil judgment (2012) Jia Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 504, it was inappropriate for the first-instance court to also dismiss Tian Yinxian's claims from that case in this proceeding. This court hereby corrects that error.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 56, Paragraph 3, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 31, 2015:

1.  Affirm item 1 of the main judgment of the civil judgment [(2013) Jia Min San (Min) Che Zi No. 1] of the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai.
2.  Revoke item 2 of the main judgment of the civil judgment [(2013) Jia Min San (Min) Che Zi No. 1] of the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai.

This judgment is final.
